_comment: What red looks like on `main`. Keyed on file+name and never on the TAP
number, because `node --test` numbers the run flat and one new test file
renumbers every test after it.
THE SET IS THE REPOSITORY'S, NOT THIS SEAT'S, as of 2026-11-02. This file
used to run `tools/**/*.test.mjs` and to CITE the repository's canonical
set beside it, recording two numbers off two sets and a note saying they
were not comparable. There is one set now: `scripts/ci-checks.mjs ->
toolingSuites()`, imported rather than re-derived, resolved from the index
at run time. `suiteSet` below records its size at the measured commit.
Widening it was window 88's named blocker and it needed one fix: the
worktree path anchor was a single segment read off the old glob, so a
failure under `skills/` or `scripts/` could not be keyed at all. It is now
an exact match against the set, with the root anchor kept as a fallback for
a suite a sibling branch added. Both are measured in the sibling test file.
A COMPLETE RUN IS ITS OWN CONTROL, and `minPoints` is not it. The floor
catches the empty run; it cannot catch the PARTIAL one, which clears it and
then writes off every debt it never reached. Measured on this host the day
this was written: a trunk run cut off at 435 of 516 points cleared the 380
floor, reported this file's one standing row as GONE, and exited 0. The
producer says whether it finished -- `1..N` and `# tests N` are printed
last -- so their absence is now exit 2 and not a note in the report header.
`minPoints` is a floor on TOP-LEVEL points (node's `1..N`), not on
`# tests`. Those are 516 and 849 here and conflating them refuses a
healthy suite; this seat did exactly that on the tool's first real run.
THE FLOOR MOVES WITH THE SET. It was 380 against a 425-point set, a tenth
under. Widening to 516 without raising it would have left a run free to
lose 136 points and still report, so it is 460 here, measured and not
scaled: 460 is under every reading this file has taken on the canonical
set and over half of it. Raise it when the set grows again; a floor that
stays put while its set doubles is a control that has quietly retired.
`owner` is established from an open row that touches the failing file,
or from git authorship of its last change, and `ownerEvidence` says
which. It is never a guess about whose lane a file looks like, and it
says UNOWNED when neither is available. The open-row half is a QUERY
and never an assertion: every row in this file's first version carried
the sentence `No open row touches this file` and three of the four were
false, because the sentence was written rather than run. The query is
in this file's sibling incident entry and it is four lines.
`dependsOn` SAYS WHAT EACH RED IS A FUNCTION OF, and it is the field
this file was missing. A baseline is a record of the trunk, so it is
only sound for a test whose result is a function of the TREE. Of the
five rows this file has ever held, zero were: one reads a host path,
three assert on `docs/ideas.md` content that seven open rows append to,
and the fifth reads the live open pull request queue over the forge API,
so its colour changes when the PM merges and no commit to `main` is
involved at all. For any row that is not `tree`, a green reading is NOT
evidence of a repair and must never be actioned as one -- see the
`repaired` block's `tools/doc-model/check.test.mjs` entry, which is the
measured case.
`minFreeMB` IS AN ENVIRONMENT CONTROL AND NOT A SUITE ONE, and it exists
because a COMPLETE run can still be invalid. Measured on this seat's own
branch on 2026-11-02, minutes apart, same commit and same set:
volume at 20 MB free    600 points, 933 collected, 68 NEW_RED, exit 1
volume at 2.0 GB free   600 points, 933 collected,  0 NEW_RED, exit 0
Every one of the 68 was in a suite that builds a temporary git repository.
Both runs printed `1..600` and `# tests 933`, so both FINISHED and the
plan-line refusal above cannot tell them apart. Completeness is a property
of the producer; validity needs a property of the environment. 512 MB is
the floor: two orders over the figure that produced the false reds and
comfortably under the 2.0 GB that produced none. It is sampled before and
after the run and the MINIMUM is what is tested, because the pressure here
is other sessions on a shared volume and it swings by gigabytes inside one
run. Two samples is not a watch, and a run can still dip between them.

suiteSet.source: scripts/ci-checks.mjs -> toolingSuites(), resolved at run time from `git ls-files -z '*.test.mjs'`
suiteSet.note: Measured on b16cbd2a, the trunk, in a detached worktree at .scratch/wt-main on 2026-11-02T09:0xZ. The first run of this measurement died mid-flight at 403 points with no plan line, on a volume that went from 3.2G to 1.4G free during the run; it was re-derived rather than believed, per the ENOSPC rule, and the complete re-run is the row above. The retired `tools/**/*.test.mjs` set gave 425 points and 711 collected on 2f89238f -- a different set AND a different commit, so neither number is comparable to these.
suiteSet.retiredSet: tools/**/*.test.mjs, 31 suites at the top level, 38 at all depths. Kept as RETIRED_SUITE_GLOB in the tool, named and not invoked, because this file's recorded history cites its numbers.

red.name: the real queue: measured on a complete clone, or skipped with the reason named
red.note: Failing on 2f89238f, measured twice. The assertion is `at least one head reads zero without repairing anything -- the class a bare count credits`, over the heads of the OPEN pull requests read from the forge API, so its colour is a function of which rows are open at the instant of the run and not of the tree. It flipped red through a merge, not a commit, and it can flip green the same way. It was not in this file's first version because that version was measured on 2a18d98f, where this test skipped.
red.ownerEvidence: git authorship: 7342e170 "security: a test's skip named a cause the clone had already repaired", author ursa-security, 2026-11-02T05:56:05Z. Open-row query run over all 16 open rows on 2026-11-02 at 08:45Z: none touches this file.
red.hostDependent: requires a complete, multi-branch clone and `refs/prs/*` fetched; it skips rather than fails when either is absent, so a seat on the host's default clone will not see this red at all.

repaired.name: transcribed: the events read refuses unknown filters, so the INERT finding was acted on
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-02T08:40Z, 29 tests, 0 failing, measured on a detached worktree at origin/main
repaired.note: A stale assertion of ours, not a trunk defect and not an HQ regression. It asserted the SPELLING /no such filter/ inside the events route's own window; HQ moved the refusal into a shared helper. Security's fix asserts the property rather than the spelling. Reads a host path outside the repository and skips itself when absent, which is why this tool has an UNRUNNABLE verdict.

repaired.name: the shipped registry has no errors for the seat that owns the files it can fix
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-02T08:40Z on 2f89238f, 19 tests, 0 failing -- AND #716 IS NOT MERGED.
repaired.note: THIS IS THE ROW THAT PROVES WHY `dependsOn` EXISTS. The test is green on the trunk and the fix for it is still open. It went green because the registry content it reads changed under it when other seats' rows merged, not because anything was repaired. So the tool's `FIXED -> drop it from the file` verdict, applied here, would have deleted the org's only record of a live unrepaired debt on evidence that measured unrelated content. For a row whose `dependsOn` is not `tree`, green means NOT CURRENTLY REPRODUCIBLE and never FIXED. The engineer's account of the defect: the test asserted `candidates equals sites flat`, which was stricter than the gate's own contract and demanded a cross-lane edit no run of this repository could make; the gate itself exits 0 with zero errors and downgrades the two unaccounted candidates to warnings because they are sections of `docs/agents/runner-facts.md`, which this seat owns.

repaired.name: every real heading that announces a scan is classified as one
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-02T08:40Z, 17 tests, 0 failing, measured on a detached worktree at origin/main
repaired.note: NOT convention drift, which is this seat's correction to accept. The block this assertion fails on already uses the standard heading spelling; it carries a first-step line, so the classifier demotes it to an idea by design, and it then satisfies all five required fields and the gate accepts it. The assertion was testing purity where the gate's property is sufficiency. Security's words, and they reproduce.
repaired.correctionNote: This row's first version said `No open row touches this file`. False: security's own #709/#719 touched it and repaired it before this baseline was written. The row was green in 277b7a45, the commit that wrote the assertion -- verified by running it there, 17 tests, 0 failing -- and red at refs/prs/715, the market seat's branch head, and at 2a18d98f once that branch's content reached the trunk. So it was never `already red at branch point` in the sense this tool's header means; the red was authored on another seat's branch and arrived by merge.

repaired.name: the real file has exactly one tag-announced scan, and it is the one measured
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-02T08:40Z, 17 tests, 0 failing, measured on a detached worktree at origin/main
repaired.note: Convention drift, and this is the one of the two that the diagnosis fits. Expected 1, got 0. The test matched `### 2026-11-02 (engineer, craft scan) --`; the file came to spell it `### 2026-11-02 (engineer, message run) -- Craft scan: ...`, with the scan word past the em dash. The test's own comment anticipated the count RISING and had no reading for it falling to zero.
repaired.correctionNote: Same false clause as the row above: `No open row touches this file` was written, not run. Same green-at-277b7a45, red-at-refs/prs/715 history, verified by running it at both.
